quest.title: The Flickering Light Splits in Twain
quest.description: The Abyss is invading, and the situation grows dire. Everyone has their mission, and here and now, you decide to first speak to Mavuika about the key information you've obtained...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Primogem x30, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

talks.objective: Return to the inn to rest
Go outside the inn to have a look

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ah, you're already here. I was just about to come get you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you're up early! That's impressive, especially after all the drinking last night...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let's... not bring up last night. I'm embarrassed about the whole thing.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, I was also woken up by the commotion. Looks like all the warriors from the Stadium are on the move.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I heard many areas have been attacked by the Abyss, including the Masters of the Night-Wind. I need to head back right away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Abyss attacked again? Are you sure you can handle it on your own? Do you need our help?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'll be fine. We also have the support of the warriors stationed at the various outposts. Given the quick response, things shouldn't get too serious.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The Stadium could always use more manpower, so you should join the forces here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about Ororon?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm done making excuses for him. He's not a child anymore. He needs to take responsibility for his actions.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I was the one who vouched for him, so I need to report back to the Speaker's Chamber. I'll accept however they choose to handle the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, I should be able to convince them to let me go back to my tribe first to deal with the attack.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: As for the Ancient Name... Once we handle this crisis, I'll talk to Xilonen right away. Don't worry — I never forget a promise to a friend.

choices.text: Be careful.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Thank you. Alright, I need to start heading back!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She left in a hurry... The situation must be really serious.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like a lot of people are heading to the Stadium. Let's see what's going on.

choices.text: I'll keep an eye out for Ororon, as well.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Over here! Perfect — our Star Outlander has appeared!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you're all here! But, uh... What's with the whole "Star Outlander" thing?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Just my way of saying how awesome you are! We've got a real emergency on our hands, so this is the perfect time for you to show off your skills.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, but can we get a quick run-down of the situation first?

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: The Abyss suddenly attacked the Collective of Plenty, the Masters of the Night-Wind, the Children of Echoes, and a number of our camps and outposts in the wild.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All at once?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yes, and the attacks are increasing in frequency.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: The tribes have plenty of defenses, so they're safe for now. But, I can't say the same for the adventurers and merchants stuck in the wild.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Chasca and I have been searching for survivors and treating the wounded. We just got back, but we need to head out again soon.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: I plan on heading back to the Collective of Plenty, just in case my tribe needs me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about you, Mualani? Where are you gonna go?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I'll go help the Children of Echoes. They're the closest, so I can start fighting right away.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: What about you guys? We could go together!

choices.text: I need to talk to the Pyro Archon first.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Yeah, that does sound important. No worries! Just leave the Children of Echoes to us!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hehe, who knows? Maybe yours truly will have the Abyss on the run by the time you're finished!

response.speaker: Iansan
response.text: That would be pretty great, actually. I hope my tribe gets through okay.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: It'll be fine! Your tribe doesn't do all that body-building for nothing!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Let's part ways here for now, and most importantly... Be careful, everyone.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: Oh, and some of us need to avoid getting contaminated by dangerous-looking substances. That will make my job a lot easier.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Chuychu, do we really have to do this now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ha... haha, it's alright! She's just looking out for everyone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, let's hurry up and talk to the Pyro Archon, so we can help the others!

choices.text: I learned a few things from The Captain.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you two. As you can see, things are not looking good right now. People across Natlan are in danger.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Look, I'm very interested in your recent adventures, but this is not a good time, so we'll have to keep our conversation short.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's alright! We're also in a hurry. We're gonna go help the Children of Echoes after this.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We met The Captain.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Mavuika about your brief meeting with The Captain and Ororon.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: So he thinks my plan is too risky. He thinks I'm being stubborn...

choices.text: Well, is it true?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I shouldn't underestimate the Fatui's ability to gather intelligence... The Gnosis does have that function, but there's more to the story.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I will answer you honestly, but you must help me keep this a secret.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I can use the power of the Gnosis to save Natlan, but it comes at a heavy price.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The Gnosis would drain all the souls and memories from the Night Kingdom and weave them into a giant net, which would surround the Ley Lines and protect them against Abyssal corrosion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you can use souls to weave a net? But, does that mean...?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Yes, it means sacrificing those souls in the process. Souls are just another form of life... The cruelty of this method is self-evident.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The Night Kingdom not only houses the souls of the dead, but also our memories and legends. Using the Gnosis means converting all three into material for the net, erasing our history and culture.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Even then, the net can still become corroded. If we cannot find a way to repair the damaged Ley Lines before that happens, then all those sacrifices are for nothing.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Given the enormity of the price, it's a solution I refuse to consider right now. I want us to win, but I also care about HOW we win, and what that means for us in the end.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Now, it's true, both plans comes at a risk, but, after weighing our options, this is our best bet.

choices.text: I'm surprised the Gnosis has this function...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Natlan is unique among the nations of Teyvat. Given the ever-looming threat of the Abyss, the Pyro Archons had to account for the worst case scenario.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Having a contingency plan is our duty... not just to the people of Natlan, but to all who live on this continent.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Still, this has always been a well-kept secret. I'm very curious how The Captain learned this information...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, one more thing... The Captain said he found another way to solve the problem. Could be equally as extreme, though...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Without the Gnosis, he should have no other option. But, I see no reason for him to lie...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Seems like our only path forward is to track him down, so he can answer that question for us.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The Pyro Archon just shared an important secret with us, and she seems sincere. Figuring out The Captain's supposed new way of saving Natlan is the key...)

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Judging by your expression, you must have doubted me, even if just for a second...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe a little.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Not even a little! We would never... Wait, what are you talking about, {NICKNAME}!?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Haha, just as expected. I appreciate your sincerity.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Maybe it was out of caution, anxiety, or simple curiosity, but know this — no matter what, our goal remains the same. We both want to save the people of this land.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: So, now that you have your answer, do you still doubt me?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Not at all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Phew, you scared Paimon! You've really got a lot of guts, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: That's a good thing. Oh, and feel free to call me Mavuika. It's what all my friends call me, and I like it that way.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: As for The Captain, the intelligence officers we assigned to the Fatui should be back soon. We'll get our answer then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's great! Sounds like we just have to wait a little longer...

choices.text: Are the current attacks...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Not just yet. Even though the Abyss is attacking several locations at once, I'm confident the warriors stationed in those areas can handle it.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Don't worry — I just need to finish coordinating our available manpower, then I'll take a small team to handle the difficult locations.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you're going to fight in person? Didn't you give up your power?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: That's true. I'm far less powerful than a god in my current state, but don't forget — I was an experienced and powerful warrior before I ever became the Pyro Archon.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: No matter how you look at it, my duty is on the front lines.

choices.text: I'm sure you're an inspiration to all your warriors.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Haha, I just think there's strength in numbers. If the people feel emboldened, that's just a bonus.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Anyway, even if we respond to these threats in time, it's not a permanent solution in the long run.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I've considered moving my people to other nations, but given their close connection to the Night Kingdom, a forced evacuation would have devastating consequences.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I've told the chiefs of each tribe to strengthen their defenses and advise people against leaving their settlements.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Now, I just need to find the right time to disclose the true nature of the crisis to the people of Natlan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's a little worried about how people will react...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think a lot of people will join the fight.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Yes, but that won't be the only response. In any case, that's for me to worry about. I'll let you know when we have more information on The Captain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, we should head out! Maybe we can join up with Mualani? She can't be too far ahead.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, let's go. Stay safe, Mavuika.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Heh, no need to worry about me.

choices.text: Sure you're not stretching yourself too thin?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Now, you doubt my strength? That hurts, Traveler. If we had time to spar, you might think otherwise.

choices.text: The beginning of the real disaster?
It doesn't sound like something an Archon would do.
Can the Gnosis do what he said?

talks.objective: Go to the Children of Echoes

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Quick, over here! To safety!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Kachina, how many people do you have left?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: They've all made it out!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: #It's {NICKNAME} and Paimon! They're here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the situation?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: There's a trapped caravan that needs our help. We need to rescue them as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: We'll go together.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I—I'm coming, too!

dialogues.speaker: Todar
dialogues.text: I... I really thought I was done for...

dialogues.speaker: Todar
dialogues.text: I can't thank you enough.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it! We're just glad you're okay. Let's see... Your goods look fine, too. Guess the Abyss isn't after Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: That should be the last Abyssal Pylon near the Children of Echoes.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Phew, that was scary, but... We did it!

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: By the way, where's Citlali? I thought she would come with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Masters of the Night-Wind also got attacked, so she went back to help her tribe. She said we can deal with the Ancient Name later.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: That makes sense. The attacks are more urgent.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Alright, this isn't a good place to talk. Let's head back to the tribe.

talks.objective: Return to the Children of Echoes

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Looks like a few people were hurt after all... *sigh* I should have got here sooner.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The Abyss threw a lot at us at once. I rushed out as soon as I heard the alarm, and there were already so many monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Before long, Kachina brought over a whole group of warriors, and just like that, we destroyed several Pylons as a team.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I wasn't in charge or anything. We just happened to be together...

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Still, I think this proves that camping in the wild was a great idea! That's how we were able to respond so fast!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Sleeping on the wet grass was pretty uncomfortable, but it was worth it.

choices.text: I don't mean to be negative...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You mean the situation in Night Kingdom, right? I feel the same way. We've managed to keep it a secret all this time, but more and more people are realizing something's wrong.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's impossible not to feel anxious when things are getting worse by the second, and all we can do is to wait.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: And we still don't know when the final two heroes are going to appear...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: That just means we need to buy the Pyro Archon more time! Keep pushing, everyone. Every battle is worth something!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You really are an eternal optimist, Mualani! You always find a way to cheer people up.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Why thank you, hehe... I guess it's one of my better qualities.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I learned a few things you should know.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You share The Captain's intel.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: ...So, specifics aside, the Pyro Archon confirmed that the Gnosis can resolve the crisis, but it comes at a huge price.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: And, somehow, The Captain finds out about it, goes to fight the Pyro Archon, and calls her out for having a solution but refusing to use it...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Honestly, if he has the same information as us, I can't really blame him...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: It's probably because our plan is so risky. We don't even know if the six heroes will reunite in time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We talked to Mavuika before we left the Stadium. According to her, the cost of The Captain's plan is too high.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And, well, it makes sense... If that was truly the better choice, she would have picked it!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Yeah, I trust the Pyro Archon. When I was upset about Kachina's disappearance, she was really sincere and patient with me.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Plus, she burned down all those precious mementos for Kachina. She's already proven how much she values even a single person's life.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: When it comes to Natlan's survival, there's no way she would hold back.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I agree. Maybe The Captain weighed the costs and came to his own conclusion, but I'm sure we have different priorities.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Life is important, but so are history and memory.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm on Mavuika's side, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As the Archon, she can't tell us everything, but it seemed like she wasn't holding anything back this time.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: The next question is... If The Captain found a new way to save Natlan, how come the Pyro Archon has never heard of it?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Yeah, and isn't he from Snezhnaya? Why would the Fatui want to save Natlan?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, this is all super confusing...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: We still don't have enough information. Once we figure out what the Fatui are doing, we'll have our answer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's head back, then. Mavuika said her intelligence officers should return soon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: With how many Fatui there are, someone's bound to give something away.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Sounds good. I have a few theories of my own. With a bit more information, we just might get to the bottom of the whole thing.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Want to join our garrison, Mualani?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: I was just about to ask! Count me in!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: If I was just a bit faster, we could have prevented a few people from getting hurt... people who could help us in the next battle. It's all a chain reaction!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Then, you should go register right away! It shouldn't take long. Everyone's looking for people!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Register? Nah, I'll just follow you around. Y'know, go where you go, do what you do...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: U—Um, okay, but then, you have to follow my orders...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hehe, you got it! I just don't wanna make the trip back. It's so far...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Alright, see you all later! Let's get together and celebrate once this is over!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you betcha!

choices.text: But, the situation is not looking good.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mavuika! Oh, Chasca and Chuychu are here... Wait! Are you okay, Chuychu!?

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: I'm fine, no need to worry...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: They ran into the Fatui while out on a mission and decided to follow them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Fatui!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Fatui wounded Chuychu?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Calm down and let me explain. Here's what happened...

talks.objective: A while ago, out in the wilds...
A while ago, out in the wilds...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Watch out. It's the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Were they attacked by the Abyss? No, wait... It looks like they're protecting a group of travelers. Over there! Do you see?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You're right. That's a traveling group from Natlan. Could they be trading for something?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Let's keep observing for now.

dialogues.speaker: Baranov
dialogues.text: We're glad you're okay. Given the appearance of Abyss monsters all over Natlan, you should cancel your journey and seek shelter at the Stadium or one of the tribes.

dialogues.speaker: Nehsi
dialogues.text: Th—Thank you so much... I wish there was something we could give you...

dialogues.speaker: Baranov
dialogues.text: We don't expect anything in return. We were out on a mission and saw you being attacked. It was our decision to help.

dialogues.speaker: Baranov
dialogues.text: If you truly wish to repay the favor, you can keep this a secret. If anyone asks, just say you were saved by warriors from Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Nehsi
dialogues.text: O—Okay, we can do that.

dialogues.speaker: Tetisheri
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Baranov
dialogues.text: We're not asking you to cover up our activities. We haven't done anything illegal. Our Captain simply wishes to remain undisturbed.

dialogues.speaker: Baranov
dialogues.text: Nonetheless, the decision remains yours. If we wanted to keep you quiet, we would have employed a harsher method.

dialogues.speaker: Tetisheri
dialogues.text: G—Got it. We'll get going now...

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Did you hear that? They mentioned a "Captain." Isn't that who the Pyro Archon is looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Exactly. We could be on to something big.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Still, there was no trade. They were just helping people in need... I didn't sense an ulterior motive.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I didn't believe The Captain when he said he wanted to save Natlan, but based on what we just saw... It's possible he was telling the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Maybe we've been wrong about the Fatui this whole time...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's too early to say. Let's follow them, and see what's really going on.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: So this is where they were headed. Looks tricky... It's heavily guarded on all sides.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Chuychu, wait for me here. I'll go in and check it out.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Oh, no you don't! How are you planning to get through all the guards?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Look, I can use this terrain to my advantage. With our tribe's special way of getting around, I doubt they'll see me coming.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: We still can't see anything on the inside. What if you can't find cover? You won't have anyone to watch your back if you go in alone!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The more heavily guarded the location, the more valuable the secrets. Even if The Captain isn't here, we can still figure out what the Fatui are planning.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: That intel is worth the risk.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: *sigh* Fine. You're not gonna listen to me anyway, so let me come with you.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: That's even more risky. You've been running around saving people for days. You're already at your limit.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'm confident I can protect myself. I'm not sure you can say the same, at least right now.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: I can.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...You really believe that?

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Fine, don't believe me, but you can't honestly tell me infiltrating a heavily-guarded Fatui hide-out all on your own sounds more reasonable...

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Y'know, growing up, even if I insisted on doing something, it never gave you any trouble. I'm not sure you can say the same...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Alright, alright, if we start arguing, this will never end. We can't let this opportunity go to waste.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Hehe, guess that means I win. Don't worry, you're not the only capable young person from our tribe. I can handle this.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Alright, same plan as usual, we split up, communicate with hand signals, make sure our blind spots are covered, and support each other once we strike.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Got your ropes?

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Yeah, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: (The Fatui have eyes all over this place. I should wait for Chuychu's signal.)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: (Now!)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Go.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: (Missed my chance. I'll wait for the next one.)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: (Not sure how many chances I'm gonna get. I need to act.)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Jump down.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: (I've been spotted!)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: (Good, I made it without getting caught. I should get to that platform over there, but it's guarded by the Fatui.)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: (Chuychu should have line of sight. I'll wait for her signal.)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: (That's it. Now's my chance!)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Quickly approach the area underneath the platform.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: (It's no use staying in one place. I should keep moving.)

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: (Looks like Chasca is helping me keeping an eye on the Fatui movements. I'll wait for her signal.)

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: (Time to move.)

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Go.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: (Phew, that was close! Almost got caught.)

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: (Probably can't make it over in one go. I'll wait for my next chance.)

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: (Now's my chance!)

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: (Haha, I made it! That'll show my sister...)

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: (Let's see... The Fatui's occupying all the best locations. If we could just get past them somehow... Wait, I've got it!)

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Toss out the mysterious sphere.

dialogues.speaker: Golikov
dialogues.text: Huh? What's that noise? Did something explode? Ugh, it stinks!

dialogues.speaker: Direi
dialogues.text: *coughing* What the heck is that? What do you think you're doing?

dialogues.speaker: Golikov
dialogues.text: I could ask you the same thing!

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: (Good, they're arguing. Looks like they just needed an excuse. They've probably had enough of this job already.)

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: (The people on the hill over there left to help their comrades. This is our chance!)

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: (Come get me, Chasca! I hope she gets this hand signal.)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: (That's Chuychu's signal... Heh, smart idea. Alright, time to move.)

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Give me your hand, quick!

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Coming!

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: I checked, and this way is completely clear. It should lead us to the deepest part of this place.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Well? I was pretty helpful, right? You know, everyone usually jumps at the chance to work with me. Not my own sister, though... No, she avoids me like her life depends on it.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I was wrong, Chuychu. You've done well.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Wait, you're just gonna admit it? Now I look like the mean one.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Let's focus on the task at hand. We're in the heart of enemy territory. The more time we waste, the more dangerous this becomes.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Alright, alright. If you're not gonna take the bait, then I'll drop it.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Looks like the Fatui are here to dig something up. I'm surprised they mobilized this many people... I doubt it's because they're interested in our culture and history.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It seems like they're looking for a dragon relic called the "Source Mechanism."

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The device is ancient. Barely any information survives to this day, and even people from Natlan don't know how to use it... Why would this be the Fatui's target?

dialogues.speaker: Yanovsky
dialogues.text: Not bad — looks like it's in good shape. This should be what our lord is looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Yanovsky
dialogues.text: Took us long enough. Come on, let's get this thing back.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Back? Back where? Should we keep following?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You really want to keep going?

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Of course! We make a good team, don't you think? No reason to stop now!

dialogues.speaker: Yanovsky
dialogues.text: Hm? What was that sound?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, we've been spotted. Time to go!

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Falling rock incoming! Watch out for your gadget!

dialogues.speaker: Yanovsky
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Yanovsky
dialogues.text: *scoff* You'll regret that... After them!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Once we got them off our tail, we went back to observe some more. They'd collected several identical pieces of something.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It looked like they were waiting, though, so we decided to come back.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: So... Chuychu got injured trying to get them off your tail?

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: ...Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: She pushed herself too hard and collapsed on the way back to the Stadium.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Well, I didn't cause you any trouble while we were fighting, right? So, my perfect record remains!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You've done very well. I could make a comment on knowing your limits, but it's not my place.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: I know, I know... I'm already reflecting on my actions.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: So, our current intel suggests the Fatui is after the "Source Mechanism."

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The device is a complete mystery, even to us. What does The Captain want with it?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I have no idea, but it's safe to assume the device could serve a similar purpose to the Gnosis.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Xilonen, I need you to gather every scholar in Natlan familiar with the Secret Source.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I'll get right on it.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Thank you both for your hard work... Chuychu, it's time for you to get some rest. Oh, and there are gifts from your patients waiting at the Speaker's Chamber.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I've prepared a small gift of my own as a token of gratitude. I'll send it to your home along with the others.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: My patients... That's so nice of them. Hehe, guess that means I'm doing something right.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: You don't need to give us anything, Archon. We were just doing our duty for Natlan. I should take Chuychu home now...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Haha, well if Chuychu doesn't want her favorite Saurus Crackers, then...

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Ah, I accept! Thank you, Archon!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: *sigh* What am I going to do with you...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: There's some for the rest of you as well. They're one of my favorites, too, so don't be shy.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'll start investigating the Source Mechanism right away. If I learn anything, you'll be the first to know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, yummy snacks!

talks.objective: Bid farewell to Chasca and Chuychu

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's next for you two?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I'm taking Chuychu home. With our parents there to keep an eye on her, I can make sure she actually rests.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Hey, it's not like I'm some kind of prisoner! I'll be fine in a day or two. There's no need to go all the way home.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: That's what you always say. Everything's "no big deal" until you collapse.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: What if the Abyss attacks again? You're saying, if I let you rest in a hotel, you're not going to rush out the minute you hear the alarm?

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: I won't! Triple promise I won't!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: Fine, on the off-chance something like that were to happen, I might...

dialogues.speaker: Chuychu
dialogues.text: But, I'm a doctor. I have a duty to help people in need no matter how hard or tiring the work gets.

choices.text: We need you.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: I guess you're right, but I don't have to like it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, this reminds Paimon of when we first met. Except you were the one trying to stop Chasca from doing something dangerous.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: I'd do the same for anyone trying to put their life in danger. As a doctor, I don't want people to get hurt because of a rash decision.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Then try to see things from my perspective. You clearly want to protect your patients, so can't you understand why your own sister would feel the same way about you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The two of you are the same, you know.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I disagree. I understand the risks and costs of my decisions.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: Who wants to be like her? Overconfident, always making excuses when things go wrong...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: That's just not true.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: *scoff* You think I don't have proof?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, okay, don't get into another fight! Just pretend Paimon never said anything.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Don't worry, Paimon. You didn't do anything wrong. Arguing is just how we communicate — neither of us really takes it to heart.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: Plus, I guess we are similar in some ways... Maybe I rush into things without thinking, but I learned that from her.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: We're family... I can't help it if my older sister is a bad influence.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Okay, you don't have to put it that way...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... you're all good now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This is probably normal for them.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Neither of us are the type to back down, so we'll always have our differences. But still, we get along in our own way.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: Plus, I know you'll wake up one day and realize I was right all along. I just need to wait.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Be my guest. Come on, let's get you home.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: #See you later, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. I'll be back once everything's settled at home.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no rush! At least grab a nice meal with your family.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: See you later.

response.speaker: Chuychu
response.text: Bye, you two! Take care of yourselves out there!

choices.text: So, you need to look after yourself, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, those two will probably make up for real at some point, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we've learned a lot. Let's go over everything that we know so far.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and Paimon try to analyze The Captain's goal. You feel like you're just one step away from the answer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Huh? Footsteps?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ahem! Sorry for popping up out of nowhere again, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, why do you look so awkward? Is there something you need from us?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Okay, I won't beat around the bush. Oh, and I'm sorry for interrupting your rest. I'll treat you to some Charcoal Grilled Steak to make up for it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome! Just give us your orders!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey, friends don't order each other around. I'm just here to share some news. Remember what we talked about before parting ways?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah! You mentioned how Ororon has always wanted to save Natlan, and something about his soul being fragmented.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon and {NICKNAME} discussed it after you left, and we think Ororon is probably back with The Captain. What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I agree with your hypothesis, and just now... I confirmed it myself.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ororon came back. He helped the Masters of the Night-Wind defend our camp.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? He came back!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did he say anything?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I told him to give up whatever he's doing, but he refused. He said they're just one step away from success, so there's no way he can back out now.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Apparently, he came back to fulfill his duty to our tribe. When he left, he said it was because he still has a duty to Natlan as a whole.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's surprised you let him go at all...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I had to prioritize my tribe. Besides, the situation was intense. I couldn't focus on outside and inside threats at the same time.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Plus, he was on guard. He knew I would try to go after him, so he made sure to keep his distance. I kept an eye out for a good opportunity, but it never came.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *sigh* All these years of calling me "granny," and I couldn't do a single thing for him in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't say that! Your tribe all raised him together, right? That couldn't have been easy.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You're right. Seeing him come back reminded me of when he was little, running around the tribe, dropping by random houses right and left...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: He's not only a child of the Masters of the Night-Wind, but a child of Natlan. It's only natural for a child to want to do something for their family.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Besides, Ororon is my apprentice. He might have a few tricks up his sleeve, but I guarantee I know every single one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what are you saying?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Look.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Remember how I said Ororon's soul is fragmented? This is the talisman I created to keep it stable.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And this gem is what makes the talisman work.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It just so happens that Ororon is due for a gem replacement. Since I can't get close to him, I put the new gem in a supply bag and asked Ifa to bring it to him.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You guys know Ifa, right? No? Well, he's a pretty famous vet around these parts. He's always bringing me all sorts of things, and he happens to be very good friends with Ororon.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ifa doesn't know what's going on, so he agreed no questions asked. Ororon would find the gem as soon as he opened the bag. He knows how important it is, so I knew he would make the switch.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: He probably suspected that I tampered with it, but here's the catch — the trick is on the bag. The moment he touched it, a portion of his memories were copied onto the old gem, which he no longer needed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's amazing! You can do something like that?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Most people can't, but I can.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That trick he used to bring you to the Night Kingdom isn't anything special, by the way. My technique is much more subtle. He won't notice anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, in other words, we have a whole backup of Ororon's memories in this gem...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph, the kid thinks he can take me on, like I wasn't the one who taught him everything he knows...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's amazing, Citlali! Let's take a look right away!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Once we get to the bottom of this, we can finally track him down.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...I know he thinks of me as his grandma, but do you think he'll get mad at me for this? You can be honest...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, that's a tough question. Paimon doesn't have a grandma, so she's not the best person to ask...

choices.text: ...It's possible. Families disagree sometimes.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: To be honest... I've always doubted my ability to look after him. I didn't stop the ceremony all those years ago, and now, I'm useless again.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: But if I stop here, it will haunt me until I'm five hundred years old. Every night, I'll wake up in a fit of anger...

choices.text: And then start crying...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Yeah, you're right. First anger, then tears... Wait! Who are you calling a crybaby?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You're just making it worse, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...I need to look at his memory. Even if he resents me, refuses to see me, or runs away for good...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I don't care, and I won't blame him. A family does whatever it takes to protect their own.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You sure you'll be okay? We can come with you if you want!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Did you just say... you'll come with me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that okay? We have a pretty good reason to see it, too, don't we? Because, uh... Right! We need leads on the Fatui!

choices.text: Paimon's right.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You really mean it?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Fine, you can come. Just promise me you'll see this through. No backing out, got it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry! We're professional adventurers.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Then, I'll place my trust in your professionalism.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Alright, time to sneak into someone else's memory and engage in some, uh... unwanted spying.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You heard it here first — I wouldn't be doing this if I had any other choice!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...*exhale* Are you ready?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm ready.

choices.text: We should be there.
And then start freaking out...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Hah, I don't scare that easy.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Still, if I back away from this and something happens to Ororon, I would never forgive myself.

choices.text: But, as his family, you have to do this.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Look how good you're doing... You'll grow into nice, big radishes in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: And you... Ifa says you're taking up too much space, but I think you're a good tree. What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Okanbi
dialogues.text: Hey! How's it going, Ororon?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Good. How are you, Uncle Okanbi?

dialogues.speaker: Okanbi
dialogues.text: Eh, can't complain. Whatcha up to? Naming your vegetables again?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No, just some idle conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Okanbi
dialogues.text: Hahaha, sounds fascinating. What did they say?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: They told me you were coming, and that you would take some produce with you.

dialogues.speaker: Okanbi
dialogues.text: Hah, only if you're offering!

dialogues.speaker: Okanbi
dialogues.text: By the way, I ran into Ifa yesterday. He told me Chasca's fostering a saurian at his place... said the thing trampled over a part of your radish garden. I hope you two didn't get into a huge fight.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No, don't worry. I'll find a way for him to make it up to me.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I've already wrapped your share of the produce. Here you go.

dialogues.speaker: Okanbi
dialogues.text: You really knew I was coming? That's pretty amazing.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Light up the smoke, and you can see the path through the shadows. That's what everyone says.

dialogues.speaker: Okanbi
dialogues.text: Hey, have you seen that strange group of people that just appeared out of nowhere?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Appeared out of nowhere... I don't think so.

dialogues.speaker: Okanbi
dialogues.text: It's the Fatui. Their leader seems like a big deal! He didn't bring many men with him, but they're all elite warriors. It seems like they're looking for someone, but I wouldn't go around asking too many questions.

dialogues.speaker: Okanbi
dialogues.text: If you run into them, be careful.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: You're from the Masters of the Night-Wind, are you not? Why do you live here alone?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: ...I enjoy living by myself out in the wild.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I guess you're from the Fatui? The one everyone's calling a "big deal"?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Not an inaccurate description.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: I'm looking for someone who may be known to you. "Citlali" is her name.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (Granny? What does an outlander want with her?)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I've heard the name. You have business with her?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: There's no point to further questioning if you insist on hiding things from me. I shall seek answers elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (He could tell I was lying, and now he's leaving? He gave up, just like that?)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Hey! At least tell me why you're looking for Citlali.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: It's none of your concern. I have my own means of tracking her down.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (Why are the Fatui looking for her? What does she have to do with them?)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (I can't just let them go like this. I have to figure out what they're planning.)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (They've just been studying the Ley Lines and asking for leads on Granny... I can definitely rule out some sort of invasion.)

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: The situation has seen no true improvement. The Pyro Archon did not fulfill her promise.

dialogues.speaker: Tarko
dialogues.text: My lord!

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Ignore him. He is no threat.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (He knows I'm following him, but he doesn't seem to care.)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (He's strong — I can tell. But there's something... unusual about him and also familiar in some way. I can't describe it.)

dialogues.speaker: Tarko
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Tarko
dialogues.text: My lord, I... I feel dizzy...

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: A Ley Line disturbance. Certain presences have been forced to wander outside their rightful realm.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (That was a spell from the Masters of the Night-Wind! How did he know that? Is he... sending those escaped souls back into the Ley Lines?)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (How did he do that so easily? Soul ferrying is supposed to be extremely difficult. This could be related to why he's searching for Granny...)

dialogues.speaker: Tarko
dialogues.text: Ahh... I feel much better. Thank you, my lord.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Think nothing of it.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Stay vigilant and continue to gather information. The Abyss could attack at any moment. If you notice any irregularities, assume drill formation and be prepared to fight.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: However, there is no reason to over-engage. Information is our first priority.

dialogues.speaker: Tarko
dialogues.text: Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (Why are the Fatui fighting against the Abyss? Do they really mean us no harm?)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (I've been following them this whole time, and still, they ignore me... Do they really not care?)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (It seems like his subordinates refer to him as "The Captain." I've never heard of him before.)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (And now, he's heading to the Stadium? That's unusual... What is he going to do?)

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: You two, with me. Everyone else, wait here as instructed. Send word to the other teams to retreat immediately if this fails.

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Yes, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (He's going inside? But, the Pyro Archon's in there... What does he want with her?)

dialogues.speaker: Tarko
dialogues.text: Forgive me, my lord, allow me to check one more time... Do you truly wish to do this?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: The time for idle observation is over. It now falls on me to act.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: This nation is out of time.

dialogues.speaker: Tarko
dialogues.text: Yes, sir.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (He just walked straight into the Stadium. What is he going to do...?)

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Hmph...!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (They're both incredibly strong. How long will they have to fight until someone comes out on top?)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (Wait, this feeling... just like the other day near the Ley Lines. It's faint, like a soul is trying to escape. Where is it coming from?)

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: (Is that why he's looking for Granny? If he dies here, then all clues will be lost. I can't let that happen!)

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: As for you... I must confess, I did not expect that little trick of yours to save the day.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No matter how dense the fog, as long as the sun remains, we cannot turn day into night. She could have dispelled it — she simply chose not to.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You don't have much time, and you're injured on top of that. What do you plan to do next?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: I'm beginning to see just how useful you may turn out to be.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: You... heard something from here, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: No need to force yourself. I've never seen anyone match the Pyro Archon in battle before.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Hm... I didn't expect you to intervene at such a critical moment.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You know I've been following you. Why didn't you stop me?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: When walking in the forest, it is only natural to encounter wild beasts. However, not every beast has the courage to come out and bite.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: And yet, one of those very beasts saved your life.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Then speak. What do you want?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I didn't save you because I wanted something.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: My soul is more perceptive than others. I can sense that the Ley Lines are extremely weak. I don't know what the Pyro Archon is planning. Can she really save us?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: The questions you asked her just now... Well, I've had very similar doubts. So, I felt like I had to help you.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: So, you can tell the truth. That was quite a reckless decision to make. I'm not sure you realize that.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: There's no turning back for me now. What I did back there is going to get me in a lot of trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You attacked the Pyro Archon in broad daylight, and I used my spell to save you. A single glance was likely all it took for her to recognize my tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: So, we're in the same boat.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: You seem to care little for my thoughts on the matter.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: It's too late for that. Start from the beginning — why are you looking for Citlali? Do you know her?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Explain your relation to her first. I know you two are acquainted. It was obvious the moment I mentioned her name.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Citlali is my elder and my teacher. She taught me everything I know. It's my duty to protect her.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: If you truly wish to protect her, you should have let me perish at the Pyro Archon's hand. Yet, you chose otherwise... Do I really need to tell you what that means?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I want to do something to change Natlan for the better, something that I can accomplish with my own two hands. You're stranger than anyone I've ever met, but maybe... just maybe, you can show me the way.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Strange...? Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Citlali... is said to be the legendary Granny Itztli, someone capable of communicating with the Wayob, and the Wayob are the key to information on the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Why do you need knowledge on the Night Kingdom?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: That is not something you need to know.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Don't forget — I saved your life.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Do you not believe the Fatui capable of betraying a debt?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: People can lie, but souls cannot. I can tell there's a weight to your soul, a sense of justice.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: You may not live among your tribe, but you certainly know their tricks. I apologize for my rash judgment... You are more capable than I imagined.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Let's go. We'll see if you have what it takes to join my plan.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: I see. Interesting approach.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Worth trying, I think.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Rather than weaving a net to protect the Ley Lines, this method would address the root problem...

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: By reconstructing the Ley Lines themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon! Are you two alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's fine! Just, um, a little dizzy...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you okay, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm just... I'm so mad at him!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *scoff* After everything, he still can't let go of the past.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can kind of understand how he feels.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: For some reason, he thinks he owes something to the people who cared for him... Heh, stubborn, self-righteous fool! Where's that gonna get him?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Now that he's all grown up, he thinks no one can tell him what to do!? He thinks he can just run away whenever he wants!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'll show him... If he tries to run one more time, he's got another thing coming!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe stubbornness runs in the family. Like grandmother, like grandson, as they say...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Is that supposed to be a compliment? Hmph, that kid's got nothing on me.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, back to what we just saw. I don't even know what to make of it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! The Captain seriously wants to... reconstruct the Ley Lines?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What does that even mean? Something like the Loom of Fate, maybe? But, how does that help with the Abyss?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: "The Loom of Fate"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... It's kind of hard to explain. Basically, it's a device from Khaenri'ah that has unbelievable power.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, if he really wants to manipulate the Ley Lines, everyone in Natlan will be affected. This is big...

choices.text: He's serious. It lines up with everything he's said before.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Which means, The Captain has been honest from the very beginning. Ororon's memory proves that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why is he so obsessed with saving Natlan? We've got to tell Mavuika about this right away!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Yes, she needs to know about this now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay, let's go!

choices.text: He tried to seize the Gnosis for the same purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Chanca
dialogues.text: Probably won't see much business today, either... Maybe I should head back and help the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Tizoc
dialogues.text: I'm worried about the situation back home. I'll write a letter to check...

dialogues.speaker: Inna
dialogues.text: Even the Saurians are getting agitated... I'm feeling a little uneasy, myself.

dialogues.speaker: Sacbe
dialogues.text: Thank goodness Xilonen showed up. That was a close one...

dialogues.speaker: Ixtli
dialogues.text: You can say that again. I can't believe this happened.

dialogues.speaker: Usukan
dialogues.text: I didn't expect Kachina to save us! She's really coming into her own.

dialogues.speaker: Yantho
dialogues.text: Of course! I mean, she already won the Pilgrimage.

dialogues.speaker: Pacal
dialogues.text: Thanks for the help. I'll take them back to the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Avilix
dialogues.text: Thank you so much for lending us a hand. I'm so glad no one got hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Todar
dialogues.text: Who knew this would be waiting for us on the other side of the desert?

dialogues.speaker: Vora
dialogues.text: Right? Just when I thought this was going to be an uneventful trip...

dialogues.speaker: Dabuya
dialogues.text: Making Mora isn't easy...

dialogues.speaker: Sadira
dialogues.text: None of the other guys who run this route mentioned anything like this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why is it so noisy outside? Paimon's still half-asleep...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... Guess we should see what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Stay safe! We've got this!
